citations.narrative:
In the puppy room, there was a ceiling tile above an enclosure housing 2 adult dogs and 1 puppy that was in disrepair.
The tile was separated from the support hinge in 2 corners and there appeared to be dust, debris, and ceiling materials
coming through a hole, approximately 2 X 3 inches in size. Dust and ceiling materials can be harmful if inhaled or
ingested by the dogs. A system should be in place to ensure ceiling tiles that are damaged or worn are repaired or
replaced for the health and safety of the animals. Housing facilities for dogs must be designed and constructed so that
they are structurally sound. They must be kept in good repair, and they must protect the animals from injury.
To be corrected by August 15, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
